canonical_proposition: Cercospora cf. flagellaris leaf spot on hemp can begin on older lower-canopy leaves as small yellow to yellow-green flecks or specks and progress to round necrotic lesions with pale centers and darker brown borders.
claim_a: Cercospora leaf spot began on older lower-canopy hemp leaves as small yellow flecks and progressed to round 2 to 6 mm lesions with tan-to-white centers, dark brown-to-purplish borders, and yellow halos.
claim_b: Field lesions in Arkansas and Oklahoma began on older lower-canopy hemp leaves as yellow-green specks and developed into round 2 to 4 mm necrotic lesions with white, tan, or gray centers and brown borders.
notes: Independent Plant Disease reports describe the same core Cercospora cf. flagellaris symptom progression on hemp. Lesion size and color details differ by report and are not collapsed into the canonical proposition.

canonical_proposition: Independent whole-plant inoculation studies support pathogenicity of Cercospora cf. flagellaris on hemp by reproducing compatible leaf-spot symptoms and recovering or reisolating the organism from inoculated plants.
claim_a: Whole-plant inoculation reproduced similar symptoms and the fungus was recovered again, supporting pathogenicity rather than visual association alone.
claim_b: Whole-plant inoculations of Sour Space Candy and Red Kross reproduced lesions, left water-treated controls healthy, and yielded the same organism; the experiment was repeated with the same result.
notes: Both independent Plant Disease reports include whole-plant inoculation evidence reproducing field-like lesions and recovery or reisolation of the same organism; the later report also records healthy controls and a successful repeat. Protocol details remain distinct.
